title: Your AI works. Will the market let you in?
subtitle: In a regulated market someone has to say yes before you can grow: a buyer's security review, a regulator, a partner, an investor. Attolloo gets early-stage AI companies ready for that scrutiny.

sections.body:
Early-stage AI companies in Fintech, Regtech, and Compliance Automation face a specific, structural problem in the 12-36 months after first product launch. They have technology that works. What they lack is the governance architecture that makes banks, insurers and other institutional buyers willing to buy it, partner with it, and fund it.

The same holds for companies that set out to compete with the established players rather than sell to them. They become the regulated party themselves, and the regulator, the partner bank and the investor ask the same questions.

+++ Why this is urgent now

The EU AI Act applies in stages. Prohibited practices have been banned since February 2025, transparency duties apply from August 2026, and the requirements for stand-alone high-risk systems now apply from December 2027. DORA has been applicable since January 2025. Institutional buyers are not waiting for the last date: they already ask for documented AI governance in procurement and due diligence. A founder who cannot document AI governance to a procurement committee loses the contract. A founder who cannot demonstrate regulatory readiness to an institutional investor does not close the round.

+++

A lawyer can tell you what the regulation says, and a CTO can build the controls. What is usually missing is someone who has run a security company and advised regulated companies through the first years of GDPR and MiFID II, and who knows what the people on the other side of the table will ask for.
sections.heading: AI companies in regulated markets do not die from lack of technology. They die from lack of governance.
Three Ways to Work Together
sections.body:
Attolloo works with a small number of AI companies, and is led by Nils Johan Brede. Most start with the first of these.

READINESS ASSESSMENT
A fixed-price review of how your company looks to the people who have to say yes: a regulated buyer, a regulator, a partner or an investor. You get a written report: the Responsible AI Gate, the 6Sense screening, an AI Compass baseline, and a 90-day plan in priority order. The report is yours to use whether or not we work together afterwards.

BOARD, ADVISORY AND MENTORING
A board seat, a standing advisory role or a mentoring agreement, for a fee agreed in advance. For companies that want governance experience in the room when the funding round, the audit or the large contract comes up.

EXECUTIVE PARTNERSHIP
Hands-on executive support in a critical period: a funding round, a licence application, an audit or a first large institutional customer. Offered by agreement, and only after an assessment. Scope, start and terms are agreed case by case.

Terms are agreed in writing before the work starts: what Attolloo contributes, what it costs, and how the engagement ends.

[Book a Readiness Assessment](/contact.html#screening)

sections.heading: AI in the Wrong Hands
sections.body:
Public anxiety about AI is rising: concern about what AI may do to society, to working lives, and — above all — what happens when AI ends up in the wrong hands. Attolloo treats this concern as a governance question, not a marketing message.

Every venture is assessed for misuse and dual-use risk before commitment, red lines apply regardless of commercial attractiveness, and where Attolloo holds equity, exit criteria govern who the technology can be sold to.

[Read Attolloo's Responsible AI commitments](/responsible-ai.html)

sections.heading: The Method Behind It
sections.body:
Every engagement uses the same four frameworks: 6Sense Filter, AI Compass, Polaris Sprints and Kando Framework. They were developed in practice and then grounded in established management theory. They have not yet been independently validated; the [Research](/research.html) page sets out what that would take.

> The 6Sense Filter opens every engagement, as part of the Readiness Assessment. If your company does not pass all six dimensions, I say so, early and clearly. The filter exists to protect both parties.

+++ What each framework does

6SENSE FILTER
Six-dimensional qualification gate. Screens for genuine market demand, a sustainable business model, operational capability, strategic focus, regulatory risk, and decision-making quality. A longer partnership requires all six.

AI COMPASS
1-to-5 star diagnostic of AI governance maturity. Maps where a company actually is, from no inventory of its AI systems and no named owner (1 star) to independently assured governance (5 stars). Prescribes a sequenced path forward.

POLARIS SPRINTS
Execution architecture and performance governance. Tracks the metrics that drive capital decisions — customer profitability, delivery performance, cash flow efficiency, and operational capacity. Ensures digital product sprints and regulatory compliance milestones move in lockstep.

KANDO FRAMEWORK
Operational execution and crisis intelligence. Applies Theory of Constraints and Drum-Buffer-Rope logic to executive capacity management. Converts negative events (lost deals, churn, complaints, audit findings) into structured strategic intelligence.

+++

[See the method applied to an example company](/example.html)
